# Independent snapshot-auth interoperability oracle

Generated with Node builtin crypto only, independently of the Go verifier. The source owner confirmed the exact header/payload field names and object-valued raw canonical snapshot before generation. Contract SHA256 is e5125bbcdc7dba1b63b8e8ae1f782f7823526dc1327472661938768de53b2f07. No dependency, repository edit, transport, credentials or production operation.

The signing seed is **published RFC 8032 section7.1 test1 data**, not an operator/authority credential and never suitable for deployment. Generation checks the derived public key and exact RFC empty-message signature before producing any vectors. [Public RFC test vector](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032.html#section-7.1). Compact signing is over the original ASCII `base64url(header).base64url(payload)` bytes. [RFC7515 Compact framing](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7515.html#section-3.1).

`generate.cjs` deterministically generates `vectors.json`, five exact byte files and `provenance.json`. No library dependencies or Go implementation are used. `vectors.json` contains 64 fixtures (8 accept, 56 reject), with expectation/reason, original Compact bytes, original header/payload byte arrays encoded as ordinary base64, original signing input, original signature hex and Node's raw mathematical signature-check result. Use byte arrays rather than UTF8 display strings for malformed UTF8 fixtures. Original unsigned-tamper cases retain the original signature intentionally. The fixture context/expectation fields are test-harness metadata, not protocol or API additions.

Acceptance oracle: use the supplied matching expected/trusted enrollment, trust generation7, explicit trusted clock2026-10-18T00:00:00Z, trusted key/window and explicit fixture policy86400-second trust/attestation limits and30-second future allowance. Per-vector `context` replaces only named top-level context members. A rejected trust-construction fixture (for example absent keyset) may fail before Verify. An outcome specifies acceptance/rejection, not an invented Go error constant or priority beyond the accepted contract.

All eight accepts must preserve exact canonical snapshot bytes. Revision strings9007199254740993 and18446744073709551615 must not traverse a floating-point representation. The canonical fixture contains absolute nanosecond record expiry, TTL0, ordered duplicate/empty TXT chunks and Go HTML JSON escapes. The generator implements only these already-normalized fixture inputs and known Go JSON field order/escapes; it does not claim a generic recordset canonicalizer. Source owner should compare the exact fixture against actual `recordset.Parse` and `MarshalJSON` in tests.

The accepted fixtures are high revision, max revision, lower revision, reordered outer fields, reordered header, renewed attestation, future issuance exactly+30seconds, and same revision/different canonical content. The last case is authentic to this pure verifier: equivocation, rollback and durable ordering remain the follower's separate responsibility. No admission adapter is supplied.

Rejections cover eight no-resign payload field mutations; correctly signed wrong tuple members; lower/higher/noncanonical/overflow trust generation; inner revision/digest/content mismatch; semantic but byte-noncanonical embedded snapshot whitespace/order/HTML; algorithm/type/key-discovery/header ambiguity; duplicate decoded payload name, null/unknown field, invalid UTF8/surrogate/trailing value; expiry/future-skew/lifetime/interval/timestamp violations; explicit unknown clock/expired trust/revoked absent key; and Compact framing/padding/unused bits/detached/extra segment/short/tampered signature.

`node_raw_signature_valid=true` does **not** mean this profile accepts: many correctly signed policy violations must reject. The nonzero-unused-signature-bits alias intentionally decodes to the same mathematical signature under Node's permissive decoder but must reject canonical unpadded base64url validation. No permissive Node decoding is used as the profile oracle. Large resource-bound cases, constructor alias/copy/race tests and complete parser fuzzing remain owner tests; these compact fixtures are not a claim of exhaustive coverage.

Reproduce locally with `node generate.cjs`. Provenance records Node/OpenSSL versions, generator/vector hashes, contract hash, public-key provenance and exact byte-file hashes. A separate verification step checked unique IDs, accepted-vector mathematical signatures, every Compact hash and deterministic regeneration. No secret values from existing files were read, and no random production signer or publication path exists.
